candidate.educational_objective: Recognize oxytocin-associated uterine tachysystole with recurrent fetal decelerations and respond by stopping oxytocin immediately and reassessing maternal-fetal status while initiating indicated resuscitative measures.

options.A: Increase the oxytocin infusion because recurrent decelerations may reflect inadequate contraction strength.
options.B: Continue the current oxytocin rate while waiting for the next cervical examination.
options.C: Pause fetal monitoring briefly to determine whether the recurrent decelerations are artifact.
options.D: Stop the oxytocin infusion immediately, initiate indicated intrauterine resuscitative measures, and promptly reassess maternal-fetal status.

candidate.rationale: Six contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes meets the ACOG definition of uterine tachysystole. Current Pitocin labeling requires electronic monitoring of uterine activity and fetal heart rate throughout the infusion and directs immediate discontinuation of Pitocin for uterine hyperactivity and/or fetal distress, followed by immediate maternal-fetal evaluation and appropriate measures. Increasing or continuing oxytocin would worsen the medication-related risk, and interrupting fetal monitoring is inappropriate when recurrent decelerations are present.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Pitocin labeling directs continuous electronic uterine/FHR monitoring and immediate discontinuation for uterine hyperactivity and/or fetal distress with immediate maternal-fetal evaluation and appropriate action. ACOG defines tachysystole as more than five contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes.

candidate.stem: A client receiving oxytocin for labor augmentation has 6 contractions in 10 minutes, averaged over 30 minutes, with recurrent fetal heart-rate decelerations. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
